bugs.description: On the very first customer message combining a booking request for two people (herself + her 8-year-old daughter) with a scheduling preference ('mejor seguidas'), the agent called escalate(reason='manual_request') instead of starting the sequential booking flow. No availability check, no clarifying question, no attempt to gather service/date/time for either person was made. The customer explicitly asked to BOOK, not to speak to a human -- there was no request for a human agent.
Multi-person booking request (mother + minor daughter, back-to-back) was escalated to a human on turn 1 instead of being handled via the documented sequential-booking rule.
bugs.root_cause: Prompt-adherence failure. agent/prompts/shared/critical_rules.md:72 (R-44) and agent/prompts/shared/booking_flow.md:118-120 explicitly govern this exact case ('un corte para el niño y un pelado para mi marido' is the example given) and mandate handling it as SEQUENTIAL single-person flows within the same conversation ('NUNCA agrupes dos personas... una cita = una persona') -- escalation is never prescribed. agent/tools/escalation_tools.py:42-63 defines escalate(reason='manual_request') with only a vague docstring ('customer explicitly asks to speak with a person, or when the bot cannot handle the request adequately') and no keyword/age/multi-person trigger list, which appears to have given the LLM an easy escape hatch instead of engaging R-44's supported flow. No guardian/minor-consent rule exists anywhere in critical_rules.md, booking_flow.md, or database/models.py that would make escalation the intended behavior for a child booking -- 'Corte de Niña' (audience=child_female) is a normal, fully bookable catalog service.

bugs.description: customer_count remained 0 after the run (final_state.customer_id is null). Because the conversation escalated before the customer_resolve middleware's normal create-on-first-contact path completed a booking, no Customer row exists for +34999000022. Not confirmed as a defect distinct from the P1 above -- listed for completeness since db_delta is fully zero.

hook_1_correct_child_service.note: Bot never attempted to identify a service for either person. Catalog check confirms 'Corte de Niña' (audience=child_female, 30 min) is the correct, available service that WOULD have applied to an 8-year-old daughter -- so the scenario was fully bookable and the escalation was avoidable.

hook_2_combined_request_handled_graceful.note: The combined request was not handled at all -- the bot escalated instead of running the documented sequential two-person flow (R-44). Both bookings were lost, not just one -- worse than 'losing one of them'.
